sections.hypothesis: Among liquid Binance spot coins, delisted ones included, those with the strongest returns over the last one to four weeks keep outperforming over the next week. Holding the five strongest equally, each only while its own four-week trend is up, rebalanced weekly, beats buy-and-hold of BTC on a risk-adjusted basis after realistic costs, including each coin's own spread.
sections.rationale: Cross-sectional momentum at one-to-four-week horizons is one of the factors Liu, Tsyvinski and Wu (2022, Journal of Finance, 'Common Risk Factors in Cryptocurrency') find priced in crypto. Proposed causes: attention-driven retail flows that chase recent winners, and slow diffusion of information across hundreds of thinly covered coins. Known weaknesses: momentum crashes when a falling market turns; much of the published effect sits in small coins that are costly to trade; and results look far better on today's surviving coins than on the coins that existed at the time. This test addresses each: the universe includes every delisted coin, a 20M USDT a day volume floor keeps out the thinnest, each coin pays a spread banded by its volume, and the absolute filter (dual momentum, Antonacci 2014) steps aside in market-wide declines. Disclosure: the absolute filter is standard in the literature, but it was chosen after the BTC/ETH trend-following results (2026-11-11) had been seen, which may have made it more attractive.
sections.rules: Daily bars for every USDT coin in Binance's archive (kestrel ingest-universe), excluding leveraged tokens and stablecoin, fiat and gold pairs. A gap in a coin's bars starts a new history (Binance reuses symbols), and nothing is computed across one. Every Sunday's daily close (UTC) is a decision. Eligible: at least 180 days of unbroken history and a median daily quote volume of at least 20M USDT over the last 30 days, judged from bars up to that close. Score: the average of each coin's rank on its 7, 14 and 28-day returns. Take the 5 highest scores; each gets 20% of equity, except that a coin whose own 28-day return is not positive leaves its 20% in cash. Trade at Monday's open: coins no longer selected are sold in full, then the rest are resized, skipping changes inside the 2% no-trade band; sells fund buys. A held coin whose bars stop is sold at its last close (a forced exit). Costs: 10 bps fee, each coin's half-spread set by its median daily volume over the last 30 days (1 bp over 500M USDT a day, 3 bps over 100M, 8 bps over 20M, else 15; an assumption, kestrel.toml [universe]), and square-root market impact. Long only, spot, no leverage.
sections.falsification: All coins, 1d, 2020-01 to 2025-10 (before the holdout), default parameters, run once. Reject unless all six hold: (1) Sharpe is above BTC buy-and-hold's; (2) P(true Sharpe > 0) is at least 95%; (3) max drawdown is no worse than BTC buy-and-hold's; (4) total return beats BTC held at the strategy's average exposure (Statistics tab), so selection and timing add something beyond holding less; (5) break-even cost is at least twice the cost actually paid; (6) at least 100 orders. Making less money than holding BTC is not on its own a rejection.
sections.parameters: top_n 5, fast_days 7, mid_days 14, slow_days 28 (also the absolute filter), min_history_days 180, min_volume_musd 20. Three lookbacks are averaged so no single one is chosen. Only the defaults are pre-registered; other values are new trials and belong in P3's walk-forward.
sections.costs: The main risk. Momentum churns: expect perhaps a third to a half of the portfolio to change each week, roughly 15-25x equity a year in turnover, or 100-300 orders a year. At a 10 bps fee plus each coin's banded spread (1-8 bps for the coins it can buy), that is roughly 22-36 bps per round trip, a few percent a year. Rule 5 is there to show whether the edge survives that with room to spare. At A$500, five positions are about 66 USDT each, above Binance's 5 USDT minimum.

change_reason: Platform bug fix, not a strategy change. v1's cost model estimated each coin's spread from daily highs and lows (Abdi and Ranaldo 2017); checked against BTC's known spread it read 21 bps (real: about 1) and charged the v1 run about 47 bps per side. It was replaced by volume bands (commit 6a6a05f) before this version was written. v1's only run also started at 2019-01 instead of the registered 2020-01. Strategy rules, parameters and pass/fail rules are unchanged; only the description of spread costs changes. The v1 run stays in the trial log.
